ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Accounting,
Concentration: Accounting
Description: The accounting major provides the tools for students to understand the accounting information that is used by managers within firms (for decision-making), by capital market participants (for valuation), and by corporate stakeholders (for monitoring and contracting). The major provides a strong foundation that prepares students for a variety of career paths, including investment banking, investment management, management consulting, and corporate finance. Students intending to pursue a career in public accounting should consider the CPA track which helps students to meet the requirements of the Certified Public Accountant (CPA) exam.

Requirements: All applications must be submitted online by December 15, 2024. Required application materials include: Application Fee ($80), Resume or CV, Personal Statement, Three letters of recommendation, Unofficial transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions you have attended, and TOEFL or PTE scores for international applicants (unless waiver criteria are met). Standardized Test Scores (GMAT or GRE) are optional for the 2024-2025 admissions cycle.
Description: The primary objective of the doctoral program in accounting is to train students for careers in research and teaching at the university level. Accordingly, the program provides rigorous training in the theoretical foundations and empirical tools of accounting, finance and economics. Students work closely with faculty in seminars and research projects. The relatively small size of the program provides an opportunity for students to have extensive interaction with faculty. Students begin to do active research early in the program. Students develop expertise in the major fields in accounting: financial accounting and managerial accounting. Students also develop expertise in a minor field such as economics, finance, or statistics. Faculty in the Accounting Department have a wide range of research interests including the role of accounting information in capital markets, corporate governance, performance measurement, managerial incentives, and taxation. The department sponsors two research workshop series and a series of occasional conferences that bring leading researchers to campus.
ScholarshipAmount: All admitted Wharton PhD students are offered a fellowship, which provides a stipend. For the 2023-2024 academic year, the stipend is $42,500.

Requirements: We seek students with outstanding academic records and strong quantitative skills. While we admit students from a variety of backgrounds, a typical student will have a strong undergraduate record in economics, mathematics, engineering, or a related field. Some students have also completed master’s degrees, and some have work experience, but neither is required.
Description: The PhD program in Applied Economics at the Wharton School is a full-time, residential program for students interested in applying economic analysis to a wide range of real-world issues. The program provides students with a rigorous training in economic theory and econometrics and helps them develop into first-rate researchers. Students in the program take courses from and engage in research with faculty from across the Wharton School and the University of Pennsylvania. The faculty are members of a number of departments including: Accounting; Business Economics and Public Policy; Finance; Health Care Management; Management; Marketing; and Real Estate. Wharton’s Applied Economics PhD program offers students a unique opportunity to focus on a particular area of applied economics while having strong connections to the broader Wharton community. Students in Wharton's Applied Economics PhD program typically focus on a specific area of applied economics that aligns with one of the fields of study at Wharton. Examples include: Accounting; Behavioral Economics; Business Economics and Public Policy; Ethics and Legal Studies; Finance; Health Economics; Management; Marketing; Operations, Information, and Decisions; and Real Estate. Students receive a degree in Applied Economics, and their dissertation must be on a topic in applied economics. The program trains students for careers in academic research, government and industry. All students admitted to the Wharton PhD Program are awarded a fellowship that covers the full cost of tuition and fees, health insurance, and a generous living stipend.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Artificial Intelligence for Business,
Requirements:
Required Documents
- Transcripts
- GMAT or GRE scores
- TOEFL scores (if applicable)
- Essays
- Résumé
- Two letters of recommendation
Concentration: Artificial Intelligence for Business
Description: The major in Artificial Intelligence for Business will combine a thorough grounding in the fundamentals of AI with a deep dive into how AI is being used in practice across a wide range of industries, including finance, marketing, healthcare, retail, and transportation. Students will be prepared to step into key roles in the AI-powered economy, whether that is starting a new venture that uses AI, joining an established firm to help them build out their AI capabilities, or investing in the next generation of AI-based companies. The major will draw on faculty and courses from across the University to offer unparalleled breadth and depth at the intersection of AI and business.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Asset Management/Impact Investing,
Requirements: The application includes: Background Information, Application Fee, Two Essays, Transcripts, Two Letters of Recommendation, GMAT or GRE Score (a test waiver is available for eligible candidates), English Language Test Score (if applicable), and a one-page Resume.
Concentration: Asset Management/Impact Investing, MBA
Description: The undergraduate concentration and MBA major in Asset Management/Impact Investing (previously called the Capital Markets and Portfolio Management specializations at the undergraduate level and the Investment Management major at the MBA level) prepares students for careers in asset management, including security analysis, portfolio management, sales and trading, and impact investing. Asset management involves investing on behalf of individuals and institutions. Asset management is a large and growing industry which offers many exciting career opportunities. The growth is fueled by the rising demand for retirement products around the globe as well as by the creation of new investment products, such as exchange-traded funds, and new investment strategies, such as hedge funds and private equity. The Asset Management/Impact Investing program provides a deep understanding of the investment process and the institutional features of financial markets. The program integrates theory and practice, and provides students with the analytical tools to analyze a wide variety of investment opportunities and to create investment portfolios that are tailored to the specific needs of different investors. The curriculum provides a strong foundation for all students interested in the area of investments. Beyond the core courses, the curriculum allows students to specialize in security analysis and valuation, portfolio management, impact investing, or quantitative finance. Our students obtain jobs in security analysis, portfolio management, hedge funds, sales and trading, financial advising, and impact investing.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Business Analytics,
Concentration: Business Analytics
Description:
The Business Analytics major provides students with state-of-the-art training in data analytics and its applications in business. The curriculum is designed to provide students with a deep understanding of the role of data analysis in business, hands-on experience with modern data analysis tools, and a clear vision of how data analysis can be used to improve business decisions. The major builds on the foundation laid in the core curriculum and prepares students for careers that require the ability to use data and analysis in a variety of business functions. The course of study is structured to have students work with a wide variety of data to address real business problems.

Students will learn how to:

- Build and interpret predictive models using a wide variety of data sets, including those with a very large number of variables (Big Data);
- Construct and analyze optimization models for business applications such as logistics, pricing, and scheduling;
- Apply data analysis techniques such as conjoint analysis and social media analytics to develop better understanding of consumer behavior; and
- Use data analytics to analyze risk and make investment decisions.

Overall, the major is designed to provide students with the kind of hands-on experience and deep understanding of data analytics that is in great demand in a wide range of industries. It provides an excellent foundation for careers in a wide range of fields, including consulting, finance, marketing, and operations. The goal is not simply to provide a set of specific data analysis skills, but to provide a deeper understanding of the kinds of business problems to which they can be applied.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Business Economics & Public Policy,
Requirements: To be considered for admission, you must submit a completed application, which includes: Background Information, Two Essays, Transcripts (unofficial are accepted for review), Two Letters of Recommendation, GMAT or GRE Score, English Language Test Score (if applicable), Résumé, Application Fee.
Concentration: Business Economics & Public Policy
Description: The Business Economics and Public Policy (BEPP) major equips students with the knowledge and skills needed to understand the economic, political and social context in which businesses operate and to formulate effective business strategies. The modern business enterprise is confronted with a dynamic and challenging environment at home and abroad. Rapid advances in technology, changing consumer preferences, and evolving national and international government policies all have a profound impact on a business’s bottom line. At the same time, corporations are being called upon to consider how they can better serve a wide array of stakeholders, including not just shareholders but also their employees and the communities in which they operate. The BEPP major prepares students to understand these issues and formulate private and public strategies that can promote both business performance and social welfare. A major in Business Economics and Public Policy is especially suitable for students who anticipate careers in finance, management in regulated industries, management in industries that are facing new public policy challenges (such as the tech industry), management consulting, and entrepreneurship.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Business, Energy, Environment and Sustainability,
Concentration: Business, Energy, Environment and Sustainability
Description: The Business, Energy, Environment and Sustainability major (BEES) prepares students for careers addressing the world’s most pressing environmental and social challenges. The major builds on Wharton's world-class curriculum with dedicated courses exploring topics that include: sustainable finance & ESG investing, energy markets and policy, corporate sustainability strategy, and climate risk management. The curriculum also allows for considerable cross-disciplinary flexibility: students can tailor the major to their career interests by choosing from a curated list of courses from across Penn’s 12 schools, allowing them to gain deeper expertise in specific domains such as law, design, or engineering.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Entrepreneurship and Innovation,
Requirements: To be considered for admission, you must submit a completed application, including: Background Information (Self-reported), Application Fee, Essays, One Letter of Recommendation, Transcripts (Self-reported), GMAT or GRE Score, English Language Test Score (if applicable), Resume.
Concentration: Entrepreneurship and Innovation
Description: The Entrepreneurship and Innovation major provides the skills and knowledge for students to pursue entrepreneurial endeavors. It prepares students for careers as autonomous entrepreneurs, in family businesses, or as innovators in established organizations. In this major, students will learn to develop and evaluate new business ideas, manage the organizational processes of a new venture, and acquire financing for business opportunities. This major is offered by the Management Department. The Entrepreneurship and Innovation major may be completed as a STEM major.
Accredidation: The Wharton School is accredited by AACSB International—The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Environmental, Social and Governance for Business,
Requirements: The Wharton MBA application requires background information, an application fee, two essays, unofficial transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate programs, two letters of recommendation, a one-page résumé, and an English language test score for applicants from non-English speaking countries. All applicants must also submit a GMAT or GRE score, though a test waiver may be requested. Interviews are conducted by invitation only.
Concentration: Environmental, Social and Governance for Business
Description: The Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) for Business major provides students with the foundational knowledge and critical-thinking skills to navigate the complex interactions between business and the natural and social environment in which it operates. The curriculum covers a wide array of topics, including the business case for sustainability, ESG data and analytics, risk management, climate finance, impact investing, and corporate social responsibility. Through a combination of rigorous coursework, experiential learning opportunities, and engagement with industry leaders, students will be prepared to drive positive change and create long-term value for their organizations and society.

Requirements: Wharton requires that you submit the following items as part of your application: Application Form and Fee; Resume/CV; Essays; Letters of Recommendation; Transcripts; GMAT or GRE; English Language Test (if applicable).
Concentration: Ethics, Legal Studies
Description: The doctoral program in Ethics and Legal Studies provides a unique opportunity for students to do research in a dynamic and interdisciplinary field. Students are trained to become leading scholars with the ability to publish in top-tier journals in a range of cognate disciplines. Faculty members are internationally recognized for their expertise in a number of areas including business ethics, corporate social responsibility, corporate governance, law and economics, and negotiation. Students may concentrate in either ethics or legal studies. Because of the interdisciplinary nature of the field, the curriculum is flexible enough to accommodate individual student interests. It is common for students to combine their work at Wharton with graduate courses offered in Penn’s Law School or Philosophy Department. The program is small by design to enable students to work closely with multiple faculty members. For additional information, please see the department’s website.
ScholarshipAmount: Fellowship covers the full cost of tuition and fees, provides a stipend, and covers health insurance.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Finance,
Requirements: The application requires submission of background information, an application fee, two essays, unofficial transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate programs attended, a one-page resume, and two letters of recommendation. All applicants must submit a GMAT or GRE score, though a test waiver may be available for certain candidates. Non-native English speakers must also submit an English language test score (TOEFL, PTE, or IELTS).
Concentration: Finance
Description: Finance applies economic theory to the problems of business and financial management. Finance is concerned with the acquisition and allocation of funds by a business firm, by a financial institution, or by a government agency. The efficient allocation of funds requires an analysis of the various sources of funds and a determination of the least-cost combination. Once obtained, funds are used to finance assets, which, in turn, are expected to generate income. The analysis of the proper balance between risk and return determines the value of the firm. Because the allocation of funds in an economy is carried out mainly through financial markets and intermediaries, the department also emphasizes the study of the functions and operations of these institutions. The department offers a wide range of courses and programs at both the undergraduate and graduate levels.

The Finance PhD program at Wharton provides students with a solid foundation in the theoretical and empirical tools of modern finance, drawing on a rigorous economic framework. Students are prepared for academic careers in research and teaching at leading institutions. The program provides students the flexibility to pursue their own research interests within the broad spectrum of topics in the field of finance. The program curriculum is enhanced by the close interaction of the Finance Department with the school’s other departments and the University’s Department of Economics. In addition, the department’s research centers, the Rodney L. White Center for Financial Research and the Wharton Financial Institutions Center, provide students with extensive resources, including data and faculty support. Students work closely with faculty, whose interests span a wide variety of topics. The faculty is consistently ranked among the most productive in the profession, and faculty research is regularly featured in top academic journals and the financial press on a regular basis.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Health Care Management,
Requirements: The Wharton MBA Admissions Committee is interested in your academic readiness, professional experience, and personal characteristics. Application Components include: Background Information, Application Fee, Two Essays, Transcripts, Two Letters of Recommendation, GMAT or GRE Score, English Language Test Score, Résumé, and an Interview.
Concentration: Health Care Management
Description: The Health Care Management (HCM) major, the first and largest of its kind, provides in-depth exposure to the theory and practice of health care management. Students gain an understanding of the complex economics of health care, its delivery, financing, and policy. Each entering class of approximately 75 students begins its study in the summer with a pre-term orientation program. Over the two-year period, students complete the Wharton core curriculum and the required health care courses. Health Care Management majors typically come from a variety of backgrounds, but many have prior experience in the field. Students benefit from the program’s close ties to the University of Pennsylvania Health System and the Leonard Davis Institute of Health Economics. Career opportunities for graduates are numerous and diverse, including positions in health care finance, hospital and health system management, pharmaceutical and biotechnology sales and marketing, health care entrepreneurship, and government.

The Wharton PhD Program in Health Care Management and Economics prepares students for careers in academia, government, and the private sector, in positions requiring a sophisticated understanding of the economics and management of health care. The program draws on a variety of basic disciplines including economics, sociology, and political science to build a set of conceptual and empirical tools for analyzing the special problems of the health care sector. The program’s faculty are national and international leaders in health economics and management research. Wharton’s health care faculty have done pioneering work in the areas of risk adjustment, the study of insurance markets, the economics of the pharmaceutical industry, and the impact of managed care and other new forms of organization on the cost and quality of care. Students also benefit from Wharton’s broad strength in management, and from University-wide resources such as the Leonard Davis Institute of Health Economics (LDI). Students completing the program will have the skills to do original, high-quality research on the management, organization, and economics of health care, and to teach in a university or professional school setting.
ScholarshipAmount: Full tuition, fees, and a $42,500 per year stipend

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Individualized Major,
Requirements: A complete Wharton MBA application will consist of the following: Background Information, Two Essays, Transcripts (unofficial transcripts are accepted for the application), Two Letters of Recommendation, GMAT or GRE Score, English Language Test Score, Résumé, Application Fee.
Description: Students may elect to design their own major. Proposals for an individualized major require the approval of a faculty advisor and the Vice Dean of the MBA Program. Individualized majors must consist of four course units not used to fulfill core requirements, the Leadership Journey, or another major. Individualized majors appear on the student’s transcript.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Leading Across Differences,
Requirements: The application checklist includes: Background Information, Two Essays, Transcripts, Two Letters of Recommendation, GMAT or GRE Score, a one-page Résumé, and an English Language Test Score (if applicable).
Concentration: Leading Across Differences
Description: The Leading Across Differences major focuses on the practical application of leadership skills in a diverse, global business environment. With a curriculum that emphasizes understanding and navigating cultural, generational, and ideological differences, this major prepares students for complex leadership challenges. Courses cover topics such as global leadership, conflict resolution, and diversity and inclusion, equipping students with the tools to lead effectively in today's interconnected world.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Management,
Requirements: The Wharton MBA application is comprised of background information (including a résumé), an application fee, two essays, transcripts, two letters of recommendation, GMAT or GRE score, and an English language test score (if applicable).
Concentration: Management
Description: The Management major provides students with the skills to motivate people, organize resources, and craft strategies to help organizations succeed. The major offers courses on topics such as negotiation, power, and conflict resolution; organizational design and change; leadership; competitive and corporate strategy; and entrepreneurship. The Management major trains general managers to be more effective leaders, and prepares students for a career in management consulting or in an entrepreneurial venture.

Requirements: A completed application for the Wharton Doctoral Programs includes the online application form, application fee, academic transcripts, three letters of recommendation, essays (including a Statement of Purpose), and a CV or resumé. Submission of GMAT or GRE scores is optional for all programs for the Fall 2025 admissions cycle. A writing sample is optional for the Management program.
Concentration: Strategy, Organizational Behavior
Description: The Wharton Management Department is a large and diverse group of scholars who are among the most-published and most-cited in the field. The Management PhD program has two areas of specialization: Strategy and Organizational Behavior. Students can choose to specialize in a micro or macro area of research, or combine the two. Our doctoral students are prepared for careers at top academic institutions and for leadership roles in business and government. They learn to conduct original research by working with faculty who are leaders in their fields.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Marketing,
Concentration: Marketing
Description: The Marketing major provides students with the necessary skills to succeed in a wide range of careers including brand management, business development, consulting, entrepreneurship, general management, marketing research, product management, retailing, and sales. The foundation of the Marketing curriculum is an understanding of consumer behavior and the skills to conduct and analyze marketing research. Building on this foundation, students may take courses in specific areas of marketing such as retailing, new product development, business-to-business marketing, and advertising management. Students must complete four credit units from the approved Marketing major course list.
Accredidation: The Wharton School graduate programs are accredited by AACSB International (The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business).

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Marketing & Operations Management,
Requirements: The application requires submission of background information, an application fee, two essays, unofficial transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate programs attended, two letters of recommendation, a GMAT or GRE score (a test waiver is available for eligible candidates), an English language test score (if applicable), and a résumé.
Concentration: Marketing & Operations Management
Description: The joint major in Marketing and Operations Management (MKOP) is designed for students who plan to pursue careers in which a close link between marketing and operations is critical. Such careers include product management and supply chain management. This major has a two-part core requirement: a marketing core course and an operations management core course. The remainder of the course work can be selected from a wide variety of advanced courses in marketing and operations management.

Concentration: Psychological (consumer behavior), Economic/statistical (quantitative)
Description: The Wharton Marketing PhD Program trains students to become leading researchers and scholars in the field of marketing. Our program provides a strong theoretical foundation in the disciplines of economics, psychology and statistics, combined with the development of rigorous empirical and theoretical research skills needed for an academic career in marketing. The two broad approaches to marketing are the psychological (consumer behavior) and the economic/statistical (quantitative). Students are expected to become expert in at least one of these two approaches and competent in the other. Students work closely with faculty, often collaborating on research projects beginning in their first year. For students entering with a bachelor's degree, the program is expected to take five years to complete. The first two years are primarily devoted to coursework. At the end of the second year, students take a preliminary examination. The final two to three years are spent on developing and writing a dissertation.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Multinational Management,
Requirements: Application requirements for the Wharton MBA include submission of background information, two required essays, transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended, a one-page resume, and two letters of recommendation. All applicants must submit either a GMAT or GRE score, though a test waiver is available for eligible candidates. Non-native English speakers who did not receive their bachelor's degree from an institution where the medium of instruction was English must also submit a TOEFL, PTE, or Duolingo score.
Concentration: Multinational Management
Description: The Multinational Management major equips students with the specialized knowledge, skills, and perspective needed to lead in a globalized business world. This major covers subjects such as global strategic management, cross-cultural management, comparative management, and the management of multinational corporations. Students will gain a deep understanding of the economic, social, political, and legal environments in different countries and regions, and how these factors influence business operations and strategy.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Operations, Information and Decisions,
Description: The Operations, Information and Decisions department is a multidisciplinary group of faculty with core interests in decision sciences and in the design and management of business processes. Our interests span both the theoretical and the practical. We apply the disciplines of optimization, statistics, and stochastic modeling to a wide range of business problems. We also use laboratory experiments, empirical analysis, and field studies to build theories of how organizations operate, and how individuals and organizations make decisions. Students may elect to focus on one of three broad areas: Business Analytics, Decision Processes, or Operations Management/Information Systems.
Accredidation: The Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania is accredited by AACSB International—The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB).

Requirements: A complete application will include: Online Application, Application Fee, Personal Statement, Letters of Recommendation, Unofficial Transcripts, Test Scores (GMAT or GRE), Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or Pearson Test of English Academic (PTE Academic), Resume/CV.
Concentration: ['Information Systems', 'Operations Management', 'Decision Processes']
Description:
The Operations, Information and Decisions department at the Wharton School is an eclectic group of scholars who are united by the goal of advancing the-state-of-the-art in our fields and by our passion for research that is both rigorous and relevant. Research in our department addresses a broad range of topics that are related to three main research areas: information systems, operations management, and decision processes.

Students in the PhD program align themselves with one of these three groups:

Information Systems: Research in this area is focused on understanding the economic and social impacts of information technology. The information systems faculty have diverse training in fields such as economics, computer science, and engineering. We are united by an interest in working on important, practical problems and a desire to use a variety of methodological approaches, including econometrics, field experiments, analytical modeling, and data mining. Examples of research topics include online social networks, crowdsourcing and prediction markets, platform-based business models, online advertising, media and technology consumption, and technology and development.

Operations Management: Research in this area studies the design and management of business processes that lead to efficient and effective production and delivery of goods and services. A distinguishing feature of our group is its strength in both analytical and empirical research. Examples of research topics include supply chain management, service operations, revenue management, global operations, and health care operations.

Decision Processes: Research in this area focuses on understanding and improving judgment and decision making by managers, consumers, and other professionals, including physicians, policy makers, and intelligence analysts. This research is primarily experimental, based on laboratory studies and field experiments and it draws on a variety of theoretical traditions, including behavioral economics, cognitive psychology, and social psychology. Examples of research topics include decision making under risk and uncertainty, group and inter-temporal decision making, fairness and trust, and moral judgment.
ScholarshipAmount: A fellowship that covers tuition, health insurance, and a stipend of $42,000 per year.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Organizational Effectiveness,
Requirements: The Wharton MBA application is comprised of background information, two essays, transcripts, GMAT/GRE score (with a test waiver option), English language test score (if applicable), a résumé, and two letters of recommendation.
Concentration: Organizational Effectiveness
Description: The Organizational Effectiveness major is designed for students interested in leading organizations through complex changes, building effective teams, and making sound, evidence-based decisions about people. The major covers a wide array of topics, including negotiations, power and politics, organizational design, and leadership. The course curriculum is designed to maximize students’ leadership potential by providing them with the conceptual frameworks and evidence-based insights for understanding organizations, and the skills and tools for leading them effectively. Students who major in Organizational Effectiveness will be especially well prepared for careers in consulting, entrepreneurship, human resource management, and general management.
Accredidation: The Wharton School, both undergraduate and graduate programs, is accredited by AACSB International - The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Quantitative Finance,
Concentration: Quantitative Finance
Description: The quantitative finance major is designed for students planning careers in the financial industry that require more quantitative and theoretical tools than a standard finance major. In addition to the core MBA curriculum, students must complete at least four credit units (cu) from the approved list of quantitative finance courses. The major provides a deep understanding of the fundamentals of financial theory and its applications. Graduates are well-prepared for roles in asset management, investment banking, hedge funds, and other areas of finance where a strong analytical background is essential.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Real Estate,
Requirements: The Wharton MBA application is comprised of the following components: Background Information, Essays, Letters of Recommendation, Transcripts, GMAT or GRE Score, English Language Test Score, Resume, Application Fee.
Concentration: Real Estate
Description: The real estate major provides students with the analytic tools and institutional background for careers in real estate development, investment, finance, and consulting. The major combines the traditional fields of finance and economics with the applied fields of development, asset management and project management to prepare students for the full range of opportunities in the field. Students learn from faculty members who are leading academic researchers and industry consultants. Students also have access to the resources of the Samuel Zell and Robert Lurie Real Estate Center at Wharton, which provides support for research, teaching, and a broad range of extra-curricular activities. Real estate majors are required to take at least 4.0 cu from the real estate course offerings. Students may also take approved elective courses from other departments as part of their major requirements. For more information, please see the Real Estate Department website and the MBA Resource Guide.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Social and Governance Factors for Business,
Requirements: The Wharton MBA application is comprised of your self-reported background information, the application fee, two essays, transcripts, two letters of recommendation, GMAT or GRE score, and an English language test score (if applicable). Applicants must apply through the Wharton MBA Program and select the SOGO MA as part of their application.
Concentration: Social and Governance Factors for Business
Description:
The Social and Governance Factors for Business major provides students with a set of frameworks and tools for understanding, assessing, and solving business challenges and opportunities associated with environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors. The major equips students to respond to the growing demands from investors, employees, customers, and other stakeholders for business to address these issues. The curriculum is interdisciplinary, drawing on faculty and courses from across Wharton departments and Penn’s schools. The major is well-suited for students preparing for a wide range of careers, including in finance (impact investing, project finance, private equity), consulting (ESG strategy, risk management), entrepreneurship (social ventures), and corporate management (sustainability, strategy, operations).

Students who wish to pursue careers focused on environmental topics are encouraged to consider the courses that will best prepare them for those roles (e.g., those on climate, energy, and supply chains). The ESG major is different from the Business, Energy, Environment and Sustainability major in that it has a broader focus beyond environmental topics.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Statistics and Data Science,
Requirements: A complete application includes the following: Completed Online Application, Application Fee, Statement of Purpose, Resume, Letters of Recommendation (2), Transcripts, GRE (Optional), English Language Proficiency.
Description: The Master of Arts (MA) in Statistics and Data Science is a terminal degree program, intended for students who plan to pursue a professional career in statistics and data science. It also provides a strong foundation for students who plan to continue with a doctoral program. The curriculum for the MA degree has been designed to provide students with training in the fundamentals of statistical theory and data analysis. Students develop a high degree of proficiency in statistical reasoning, computational skills, and the art of data analysis, providing them the flexibility to apply their knowledge to a wide variety of application areas. The MA in Statistics and Data Science program is a STEM-designated program.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Statistics and Data Science,
Department: The Wharton School, Graduate School of Arts & Sciences
Concentration: Statistics and Data Science
Description: The Statistics and Data Science major provides students with a solid foundation in statistical thinking and a deeper understanding of data science models. These techniques are used to analyze financial data, evaluate marketing campaigns, and predict business outcomes. Students who take this major will learn skills that will enable them to contribute to and lead teams of data scientists as well as to bring an evidence-based, data-centric culture to all aspects of an enterprise. The major also prepares students for more advanced or specialized studies at the doctoral level. While the major is a valuable standalone option for students, the major is designed to be easily accessible to students who are also pursuing another major, allowing students to combine the data analytic skills gained through the major with an application domain (e.g. accounting, finance, marketing, etc). The major is an attractive option for students interested in careers involving data analytics and business intelligence, as well as those on a finance, consulting, technology or general management track.

Requirements: Applicants to the doctoral program in Statistics and Data Science must apply online. Completed applications and all supporting material must be submitted by the deadline of December 15.
Description: The Doctoral Program in Statistics and Data Science at the Wharton School is devoted to the development of statistical and data scientific theory and methods, and their application to a wide range of fields. The program is flexible and offers training for a variety of career objectives. Students may go on to careers in academia, in industry, or in government. Graduates of the program who have chosen academic careers hold positions in some of the most prestigious universities in the world. Recent graduates taking jobs in industry now hold positions at major financial firms as well as in cutting-edge technology companies. The faculty in Statistics and Data Science have diverse interests and are internationally renowned for their research. Students work closely with faculty, participating in research seminars from their very first year in the program. Many become involved in research projects with faculty at a very early stage of their studies. The PhD program offers a number of courses in advanced topics in statistics and data science, and students may also take courses in other departments. Coursework is chosen by the student with the guidance of a faculty advisor.

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Strategic Management,
Requirements: The application includes background information, two required essays, a one-page resume, transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate programs attended, and two letters of recommendation. A GMAT or GRE score is also a component, but applicants may request a test waiver. An English language test score (such as TOEFL or PTE) is required for non-native English speakers who did not earn a degree from an institution where English was the language of instruction.
Concentration: Strategic Management
Description: The Strategic Management major provides the concepts and skills for developing strategy and managing organizations. Strategic management is an integrative field, and it builds on a foundation of core business disciplines. Students who major in Strategic Management may pursue a wide range of career options, including management consulting, corporate staff positions in planning and development, and line management positions that involve significant strategic responsibilities.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Africana Studies,
Concentration: Global Africa and the Diaspora, Gender, Sexuality and Women's Studies, Urban Studies, Law and Society
Description: The Africana Studies major is an interdisciplinary major in the humanities and social sciences that is designed to provide students with an understanding of the history, culture, and social realities of people of African descent. Majors in Africana Studies are expected to develop a sophisticated understanding of the theoretical and methodological issues that inform the field. They are also expected to demonstrate a solid familiarity with the key historical moments, intellectual movements, and social struggles that have shaped the discipline. The Africana Studies major requires a minimum of 14 course units. We encourage students to double-major, as Africana Studies provides a unique perspective to students who major in other disciplines, from English to Economics, and from Psychology to Biology.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Ancient History,
Requirements: Prospective students must apply using the Common Application or the Coalition Application. The application must include the Penn-specific Supplement with its required essays, an official high school transcript, a School Report, one letter of recommendation from a school counselor, and two letters of recommendation from teachers. Standardized test scores (either SAT or ACT) are also required. Reports such as the Mid-Year Report and Final Report are required when available.
Concentration: ['Greek and Roman history', 'Near Eastern history']
Description: The major in ancient history is an interdisciplinary major, sponsored by the Departments of Classical Studies and History. All majors are assigned an advisor from one of the two departments and should consult with their advisor on a regular basis. The major is an appropriate background for many fields and professions, including law and medicine, and for graduate work in history, classics, archaeology, and other related disciplines. There are two concentrations, one in Greek and Roman history, the other in Near Eastern history.

Concentration: Archaeology Concentration, Biological Anthropology Concentration, Cultural and Linguistic Anthropology Concentration, Medical Anthropology and Global Health Concentration
Description: The Anthropology major introduces students to the comparative study of human diversity and the critical analysis of the concept of "culture." The discipline is conventionally divided into four sub-fields: cultural anthropology, linguistic anthropology, biological anthropology, and archaeology. At Penn, we offer courses in all four sub-fields as well as in medical anthropology. Students may choose to concentrate in any one of the following four areas: Archaeology, Biological Anthropology, Cultural and Linguistic Anthropology, or Medical Anthropology and Global Health.

Concentration: Design Concentration, Intensive Major
Description: The undergraduate major in architecture is a liberal arts degree in the College of Arts and Sciences. The major gives students a deep and broad understanding of architecture as a cultural practice. Students learn about architecture’s history, theories and technologies in the context of global cultures. They also become proficient in the skills needed to represent architectural ideas, including drawing, modeling, and digital software. With its strong and diverse curriculum, the major prepares students for graduate studies in architecture and its allied disciplines of landscape architecture, urban planning and historic preservation. It also provides a strong foundation for students who want to pursue careers in a wide range of fields from law and business to engineering, public policy and the visual arts.

Requirements: Application requirements are for admission to the undergraduate school (College of Arts and Sciences) rather than directly to the major. Key components include: The Common Application or Coalition Application, Powered by Scoir; Penn-specific Application Essay; Official High School Transcript; School Report; Letters of Recommendation (1 from a counselor and 2 from teachers); Mid-Year Report; and the Final Report for enrolling students. Standardized test scores (SAT/ACT) are optional for the 2024-25 application cycle.
Description: Biochemistry is the study of the chemistry of life. It provides the foundation for the revolutionary developments in biotechnology and genetic engineering that are having a major impact in areas ranging from medicine to forensics to bioremediation. Biochemistry majors study the major classes of biological molecules: proteins, nucleic acids, lipids and carbohydrates. They learn the chemical principles that underlie the function of these molecules in the processes that sustain life. All biochemistry majors do a two-semester research project with a faculty preceptor. The major is appropriate for students interested in careers in the biological and chemical sciences as well as in the health professions. There is a BS and a BA version of the major. The BA degree is designed for students who want a somewhat less intensive science program than the BS biochemistry major, perhaps because they want to combine it with a second major or because they want more elective time for other courses, perhaps in the arts and humanities. The BA degree can also serve as preparation for careers in industry or public service.

The Bachelor of Arts (BA) with a major in Biology is intended for students who are interested in biology but do not plan to attend graduate school in the life sciences or a health professions school. Students in the College of Arts and Sciences may complete a major in Biology for the BA degree. The requirements are distinct from those for the Bachelor of Arts degree with a major in Biology that may be completed by students in the College of Liberal and Professional Studies. Requirements for the major are listed below. In addition, students must complete the General Requirement of the College of Arts and Sciences.

Requirements: To apply for undergraduate admission at the University of Pennsylvania, prospective students must submit the following: The Common Application or Coalition Application, a Penn-specific Essay, Official High School Transcript, School Report, a Counselor Recommendation, and two Teacher Recommendations. A Mid-Year Report is required for all admitted students, and a Final Report is required for all enrolling students. As of the 2024-2025 application cycle, applicants are required to submit either SAT or ACT scores. An interview is optional and offered based on availability. Applicants with a background in fine arts may also submit an optional supplement.
Description: Biophysics is an interdisciplinary field that applies the theories and methods of physics, chemistry, and mathematics to understand how biological systems work. Its scope is vast, covering all scales of biological organization, from the single molecule to the cell, from the organism to the ecosystem. Biophysics has grown very rapidly in recent years, leading to new opportunities for careers at the cutting edge of science. Undergraduates who major in biophysics at Penn can participate fully in this excitement through research. They will acquire a solid foundation in the physical and life sciences that will prepare them for a variety of careers in scientific research, medicine, and the biotechnology industry. The Biophysics Major is appropriate for students who are planning graduate study in biophysics or a related area, such as molecular biology or neuroscience, or the professional schools of medicine, dentistry, or law.

Requirements: Prospective students apply to one of Penn’s four undergraduate schools, not to a specific major. The application requirements are for admission to the university's undergraduate program. The required components include: The Common Application or Coalition Application, Penn-specific Essays, Official High School Transcript, School Report, Counselor Recommendation, two Teacher Recommendations, Mid-Year Report, Final Report (for admitted students), and an application fee or fee waiver.
Description: The Department of Chemistry offers several majors to accommodate student interests. The Bachelor of Arts (BA) major is less intensive than the Bachelor of Science (BS) majors and is designed for those students who desire a strong background in chemistry but who do not intend to pursue graduate school in chemistry. The BA in chemistry is also an excellent option for those who have a double major. In addition to chemistry majors, we also offer submatriculation programs for master’s degrees in chemistry and in education, as well as a minor in chemistry.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Cinema and Media Studies,
Requirements: To apply as a first-year student, applicants must submit the Common Application or Coalition Application, a Penn-specific Essay, an official High School Transcript, a School Report, a Counselor Recommendation, two Teacher Recommendations, a Mid-Year Report, and a Final Report upon enrollment.
Description: The undergraduate program in Cinema and Media Studies provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the history, theory, and aesthetics of moving images. Students learn to analyze film, television, and new media in a variety of contexts, considering their formal properties as well as their relationship to culture, society, and technology. The major emphasizes critical thinking, close analysis, and strong writing skills. Courses cover a wide range of topics, including silent cinema, Hollywood genres, international film movements, documentary, animation, television studies, and digital media. Students have the opportunity to explore filmmaking through production courses and to gain practical experience through internships. The program prepares students for careers in the film and media industries, as well as for graduate study in related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Classical Studies,
Requirements: To apply, prospective students must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition Application. The application must include Penn-specific essays, an official high school transcript, a school report, three letters of recommendation (one from a counselor and two from teachers), a Mid-Year Report, and a Final Report upon completion of the academic year. An application fee or fee waiver is also required. Standardized test scores (SAT/ACT) are optional for the 2024-25 admissions cycle.
Concentration: Classical Languages and Literature, Classical Civilization, Ancient History, Mediterranean Archaeology
Description: The Classical Studies major offers a multi-disciplinary approach to the study of the ancient Greek and Roman worlds, allowing students to explore the interconnected cultures of the ancient Mediterranean. Students in the Classical Studies major can take courses in the art, archaeology, history, literature, and philosophy of the ancient Greek and Roman worlds, and can also study the ancient Greek and Latin languages. Because of the multi-disciplinary nature of the major, students who major in Classical Studies will learn how to synthesize a wide variety of evidence (textual, material, visual, etc.) and thus prepare themselves for a wide range of future careers.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Cognitive Science,
Concentration: Language; Mind, Brain and Behavior; Cognitive Neuroscience; Computation and Cognition; Psychology: Mind, Brain and Behavior; Language and the Mind
Description: Cognitive Science is the study of the mind and its processes. It is an interdisciplinary field, combining results and insights from psychology, computer science, linguistics, philosophy, and neuroscience. Work in cognitive science has had a major impact on our understanding of language, perception, action, memory, reasoning, decision making, emotion, and consciousness; it has also led to the design of intelligent systems that can perform complex tasks that formerly required human intelligence.

Requirements: Application requirements are for admission into the undergraduate school (College of Arts and Sciences), not the specific major. Applicants must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition Application. Required materials include Penn-specific essays, an official high school transcript, a school report, three letters of recommendation (one from a counselor and two from teachers), and a Mid-Year Report. Admitted students must submit a Final Report. For the application cycle for Fall 2025 entry and beyond, applicants are expected to submit ACT or SAT scores.
Concentration: Communication and Public Service (ComPS), Communication, Culture, and Media, Political Communication, Data and Network Science, Critical Journalism
Description: The undergraduate program in Communication is rooted in the liberal arts tradition, providing a broad understanding of the role of communication in society, and a critical framework for analyzing communication institutions, processes, and effects. The curriculum is designed to help students think systematically about communication and to express those thoughts clearly. Courses in the major examine communication from a variety of theoretical and methodological perspectives. They offer students the knowledge and analytical skills to understand and evaluate communication theories and research. Communication majors have the option of selecting a concentration within the major.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Comparative Literature,
Requirements: Application requirements are for general first-year admission to the University of Pennsylvania's undergraduate schools, as students declare their major after matriculating. The application checklist includes: The Common Application or Coalition Application, Penn-specific essays, official high school transcript, school report, counselor recommendation, two teacher recommendations, mid-year report, final report, and an application fee or fee waiver. For the 2024-25 application cycle, submission of SAT or ACT scores is optional.
Description: The major in Comparative Literature allows students to bring together their passion for the literatures and cultures of different parts of the world. As a discipline, Comparative Literature is founded on the belief that literary texts can only be fully understood in a comparative framework. This means that at Penn, students not only take courses in a variety of literary traditions, they also learn how to think comparatively about what they read. The major has two main components: coursework in Comparative Literature and coursework in two foreign literature departments. In their Comparative Literature courses, students learn how to analyze and compare texts from a variety of theoretical, historical, and generic perspectives. In their foreign literature courses, students develop the in-depth knowledge of individual literary traditions and languages that all true comparative work requires. The flexibility of the major allows students to shape their own program of study in consultation with the undergraduate chair.

Requirements: Prospective students apply to one of Penn’s four undergraduate schools, in this case, the College of Arts & Sciences. The application requirements are managed by the central undergraduate admissions office. The required application materials include: The Common Application or Coalition Application, Penn-specific Essay, Official High School Transcript, School Report, Counselor Recommendation, Two Teacher Recommendations, Mid-Year Report, Final Report, and a $75 application fee or fee waiver. For students applying through the Early Decision program, the Early Decision Agreement is also required.
Description: The Criminology major is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the problem of crime and the criminal justice system. The curriculum draws on a wide variety of disciplines, including Criminology, Sociology, History, Law, and Political Science. The major is designed for students interested in studying the causes and consequences of crime, the structure and function of the criminal justice system, and the social, cultural, and political contexts of law and justice. The major provides a strong foundation for students interested in careers in law, criminal justice, public policy, and social service, as well as for graduate study in Criminology, Sociology, or Law.

Requirements:
The following is a list of all the required application materials for first-year applicants:

- Common Application or Coalition Application, Powered by Scoir
- Penn-specific Application Essay
- Official high school transcript
- School Report
- Counselor Recommendation
- Two Teacher Recommendations
- Mid-Year Report
- Final Report
- Standardized test scores (optional for 2024-25 admissions cycle)
- $75 application fee or fee waiver
Concentration: Art, Technology, and the Future; City and Social Change; Communication, Information, and Media; Mind and Materiality
Description: The undergraduate major in Design leads to a BA degree in the College of Arts and Sciences. The major combines hands-on-making with a critical and historical framing of design. The major emphasizes critical thinking and creative production and offers a curriculum that is both broad and deep, allowing students flexibility to follow their own interests and develop a unique course of study. The major requires 13 courses: five core courses in design and four courses in a specific concentration that builds on the foundations of the core. Two studio courses and two seminar/lecture courses in a concentration provide students with depth and a critical framework for understanding their work. Two additional electives, from any concentration, and two major-related courses, complete the major. Students take a final thesis course in the fall of their senior year. This course prepares them for a capstone project that is presented to the public in a final exhibition at the end of the spring semester.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Earth and Environmental Science,
Requirements: Application requirements are not specified for the major directly. Students apply to one of Penn's undergraduate schools, in this case, the College of Arts & Sciences. The general first-year application requirements include: Common Application or Coalition Application, Penn-specific Application Essay, Official High School Transcript, School Report, Counselor Recommendation, two Academic Teacher Recommendations, a Mid-Year Report, and an application fee or fee waiver. Standardized test scores are optional.
Description: The major in Earth Science focuses on the Earth as a complex system, and includes a solid foundation in the core disciplines of geology, biology,chemistry, and physics. The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Earth and Environmental Science is intended for students who wish to pursue a career or graduate work in environmental policy, environmental law, management, journalism, or education. It provides a broad background in Earth and Environmental Science, and some flexibility in the selection of upper-level courses.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in East Asian Languages and Civilizations,
Requirements: All prospective students apply to the University of Pennsylvania using the Common Application or Coalition Application. The application must include: an official high school transcript, a school report, letters of recommendation (one from a counselor and two from teachers), and a mid-year report. If applying through Early Decision, an Early Decision Agreement is also required. A final report is required for all matriculating students.
Concentration: China, Japan
Description: The major in East Asian Languages and Civilizations (EALC) provides students with a broad and deep understanding of the cultures of East Asia (China, Japan, and Korea). The curriculum is designed to provide students with the linguistic competency, disciplinary methodology, and factual knowledge to pursue a professional career or graduate studies in a field related to East Asia. The program has three key components: language training, broad foundational coursework in the humanities and social sciences, and a specialization in one area of East Asian studies. In consultation with the undergraduate chair, students build a program of study that is at once comprehensive and tailored to their own intellectual interests. The language component requires four years of Chinese, Japanese, or Korean. The foundational coursework gives students a broad overview of the history, literature, and cultures of East Asia. The specialization gives students the opportunity to bring their linguistic and disciplinary training to bear on one particular area of interest. In order to achieve the goals of the major, students are required to take a minimum of sixteen courses: eight in language and eight in non-language content courses. These requirements are described in more detail below. Students are encouraged to take advantage of Penn’s many study abroad programs, as well as the full range of courses in EALC and related departments and programs.

Concentration: Advanced Theory Concentration, Data Analytics Concentration, Finance Concentration, International Economics Concentration, Public Policy Concentration, Behavioral Economics Concentration, Strategic Management Concentration, Individualized Concentration
Description: The undergraduate economics major is designed to provide students with a firm grounding in modern economic theory, statistical and econometric methods, and their applications. It is designed to be flexible, allowing students to construct a program of study that suits their interests and goals. Students in the major may go on to graduate school in economics, law, medicine, or business; others take jobs in government, private firms, or the non-profit sector. An important part of the economics major is the senior research requirement, in which students have an opportunity to engage in economic research under the supervision of a faculty member.

Requirements: First-year applicants to the University of Pennsylvania must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition Application, which includes a Penn-specific Essay. Required documents include an Official High School Transcript, a School Report, one Counselor Recommendation, and two Teacher Recommendations. Applicants must also submit a Mid-Year Report. A Final Report is required for all students who enroll.
Concentration: American Literature and Culture, British and Other Anglophone Literature, Cinema and Media Studies, Creative Writing, Generalist, Genre and Poetics, Global and Transnational English, Literature and Culture before the 17th Century, Literature and Culture from the 17th Century to the Present, Theoretical and Cross-Cultural Studies
Description: The English major at Penn offers an opportunity to study a rich variety of literary, cultural, and historical documents, from ancient epics to contemporary films. Our department includes many distinguished scholars who are also dedicated teachers. Our courses are typically small and stress active student participation. Students are encouraged to develop their own interests and to work closely with faculty members in directed readings and honors projects. The major itself combines a focus on traditional historical fields with a wide range of theoretical and interdisciplinary pursuits. It has long enjoyed an international reputation in areas such as Renaissance literature, American literature, modernism, and contemporary poetry. It has also emerged as a vital center for the study of ethnic literature, gender and sexuality studies, cultural studies, and critical theory. The English major helps students to become perceptive readers, critical thinkers, and strong writers—skills that provide a foundation for careers in a wide range of professions, including law, business, publishing, journalism, education, and the arts.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Environmental Studies,
Concentration: ['Environmental Biology', 'Environmental Policy', 'Earth Science', 'Sustainability and Environmental Management', 'Environmental Humanities', 'Global Environmental Systems', 'Individualized Concentration']
Description: The Environmental Studies major provides students with the intellectual and practical tools to understand and address pressing environmental challenges. The major attracts a diverse group of students who are curious about the many intersections between human societies and the biophysical environment, and prepares them to pursue careers in a wide array of fields. The interdisciplinary nature of the major enables students to integrate knowledge from across the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences, and our emphasis on experiential learning—including field courses, undergraduate research, study abroad, internships, and civic engagement—gives students hands-on opportunities to apply their knowledge. Students in the major select one of seven concentrations, each of which has a distinct curriculum and area of focus. We also offer a General major option for students with an interest in Environmental Studies but whose academic interests do not fit well with any of the defined concentrations. All Environmental Studies majors take an introductory course (ENVS 1000), a statistics course, and a senior seminar in which they complete an independent research project that integrates their coursework with their concentration. For College students, the Environmental Studies major fulfills the Natural Science & Math requirement of the Sector Requirement.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Fine Arts,
Requirements: General application requirements for first-year applicants include: The Common Application or Coalition Application, Penn-specific Essay, Official High School Transcript, School Report, Counselor Recommendation, two Teacher Recommendations, Mid-Year Report (due after first-marking period grades are available), and a Final Report for admitted students who choose to enroll. An application fee or fee waiver is also required. For applicants to the College of Arts & Sciences with an interest in Fine Arts, an optional portfolio of artwork may be submitted as a supplement to the application.
Description: The undergraduate major in Fine Arts is intended for students who wish to pursue a rigorous liberal arts education and a studio-based visual arts curriculum. Students may work in a variety of disciplines, including animation and 3D modeling, drawing, painting, photography, printmaking, sculpture, and video. Through a combination of core studios, art history courses, and a wide array of studio electives, the curriculum provides an open intellectual framework that allows for a deep and broad-based investigation into the practice of making art today.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Francophone, Italian and Germanic Studies,
Description: The major in Francophone, Italian and Germanic Studies (FIGS) allows students to study the cultures of the French-, Italian- and German-speaking worlds from a comparative and interdisciplinary perspective. This major is ideal for students with an interest in two of these three areas. A major that combines two of the three subjects allows students to develop an intercultural perspective that enhances their understanding of both fields. The FIGS major consists of twelve courses, six in a primary language and culture and four in a secondary language and culture, plus two additional electives that can come from either area. In consultation with the FIGS advisor, each student will design a course of study that reflects their interests in the language, literature, history and culture of the Francophone, Italian and German-speaking worlds. Courses are taught in English and in the target languages. FIGS majors who wish to study abroad are encouraged to do so and can count courses taken abroad toward their major requirements.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Gender, Sexuality, & Women's Studies,
Concentration: Feminist Studies, Global Gender and Sexuality Studies, Health and Disability, Individualized Concentration
Description: The undergraduate program in Gender, Sexuality, and Women’s Studies (GSWS) offers students the opportunity to pursue interdisciplinary study in a variety of fields concerned with gender, sexuality, and women. Students learn to think critically about the social construction of gender and the ways in which gender and sexuality have been defined and have operated in various historical and cultural contexts. The major is broadly interdisciplinary and requires students to take courses in the humanities, social sciences, and policy-oriented fields. The GSWS major is flexible, with a required core of introductory, theory, and research courses and many options for electives in several areas of concentration.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Health and Societies,
Concentration: Bioethics and Society, Disease and Society, Gender, Sexuality and Health, Global Health, Health Care Markets and Finance, Health Policy and Law, Race, Ethnicity and Health
Description: The Health and Societies (HSOC) major provides students with a multi-disciplinary framework for understanding the social, cultural, political, economic, and ethical dimensions of health, illness, and medical care in human societies, past and present. The curriculum is designed to help students think critically about the complex relationships that link health to social and cultural contexts. All students majoring in Health & Societies choose a concentration within the major. Concentrations enable students to acquire a deeper understanding of a specific facet of the major and to hone their analytical skills by working closely with a faculty member in their area of interest. Concentrations consist of four courses. Students also complete a capstone course in their senior year.
ScholarshipType: Need-based (including Penn Grant, Federal Pell Grant, FSEOG, State Grants)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Hispanic Studies,
Concentration: Portuguese and Brazilian Studies
Description: The major in Hispanic Studies offers a broad and comprehensive curriculum in the literatures and cultures of the Spanish-speaking world: Spain, Latin America and the U.S. Courses are taught in Spanish. The curriculum combines broad survey courses with more specialized courses on specific topics, periods, authors and genres. Students are required to develop a comprehensive knowledge of Hispanic literatures and cultures from the Middle Ages to the present, as well as the analytical skills to engage critically with primary and secondary texts. Students majoring in Hispanic Studies also have the option of declaring a concentration in Portuguese and Brazilian Studies, which provides a more specialized curricular path including two required courses and several electives.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History of Art,
Requirements: First-year applicants must submit the Common Application or Coalition Application, a Penn-specific Essay, an official high school transcript, a school report, one counselor recommendation, two teacher recommendations, a Mid-Year Report, and a Final Report. An interview is optional.
Concentration: Architecture Concentration, General History of Art Concentration, Museums, Markets and Collecting Concentration, History of Art Honors Program with Thesis
Description: The History of Art major is intended to provide students with a broad and deep understanding of the history of art and architecture of a variety of periods and geographical areas, and to equip them with the tools of visual and historical analysis necessary to make a contribution to the field. Majors are encouraged to pursue an interdisciplinary and global course of study and to take advantage of the rich offerings across the university as they craft a personalized program of courses that will culminate in a capstone seminar. The capstone seminar is an intensive research and writing course designed to familiarize students with the most advanced methods in the discipline and to produce a substantial research paper. For students considering graduate work in the field, for those interested in museum or gallery work, and for those who simply wish to explore a particular area of art history in depth, the department offers a variety of specialized concentrations, as well as an honors program that provides an in-depth and challenging course of study.

Requirements: Prospective students apply to one of Penn’s four undergraduate schools, not to a specific major. The general application requirements for first-year applicants include: The Common Application or Coalition Application, Penn-specific Essays, Official High School Transcript, School Report, Counselor Recommendation, two Teacher Recommendations, Mid-Year Report, and Final Report. Standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are also required.
Description: The History Major is designed to stimulate and gratify students' curiosity about the past, to sharpen their critical and analytical skills, and to provide them with intellectual perspectives that will be of great value whatever their future pursuits. Students have maximum freedom in the choice of their courses, but the Major's requirements are meant to ensure that their choices are both coherent and broad. We especially want our students to think about the nature of history itself. The Proseminar, the Research Seminar and the optional Honors Thesis all emphasize historiographical issues as well as research methods.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Individualized Major,
Description: The Individualized Major allows students to combine courses from several departments and programs into a coherent field of study not represented in any of the College’s established majors. The major is interdepartmental and interdisciplinary in nature. A student must have a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above to apply for an Individualized Major. Students interested in this major should meet with a College advisor to discuss their ideas and to begin to search for a faculty advisor. The application to the major should be submitted by the end of sophomore year.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in International Relations,
Requirements:
Prospective students apply to the University of Pennsylvania's undergraduate program, not to the specific major. The general application requirements include:
- Common Application or Coalition Application
- Penn-specific Essay
- Official High School Transcript
- School Report
- Counselor Recommendation
- Two Teacher Recommendations
- Mid-Year Report
- Standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are optional for the 2024-25 admissions cycle.
Concentration: Commercial & Legal Institutions of the World Economy Track, Conflict & Security Track, Foreign Policy & Diplomacy Track, Global Governance & International Organizations Track, Global Health & Environment Track, International Political Economy & Development Track, Latin American & Caribbean Studies Track, Middle Eastern & North African Studies Track, Russian & East European Studies Track, South Asian Studies Track, Sub-Saharan African Studies Track, United States in the World Track, Western European Studies Track
Description: The International Relations (IR) Program at Penn is an interdisciplinary major in the College of Arts and Sciences that is jointly administered by the Political Science Department and the Lauder Institute. We offer an undergraduate education in world politics that is balanced, comprehensive, and rigorous. Students investigate the political, economic, and cultural interactions of a wide range of state and non-state actors at the local, national, and international levels. Students become familiar with the historical evolution of the international system and its current-day workings while engaging questions of ethics, justice, and the distribution of power. The IR major requires that students demonstrate a proficiency in a foreign language and complete a study abroad experience. In addition, we encourage our students to seek out internships that will help them gain first-hand experience in a variety of international fields and professions.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in International Studies,
Concentration: ['Africa', 'Asia', 'Europe', 'Latin America']
Description: The International Studies Major (ISMA) is a joint major with the Wharton School that provides students with the opportunity to combine a business education with a liberal arts focus on international studies. Students complete the full Wharton curriculum as well as 14-course units in the College of Arts & Sciences. These courses include language proficiency as well as area studies and international relations coursework. The major allows students to choose a concentration in a particular geographic region of the world: Africa, Asia, Europe, or Latin America. This joint major is only open to students admitted to the Huntsman Program.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Jewish Studies,
Requirements: Application requirements are not specific to the Jewish Studies, BA major but are for general undergraduate admission to the College of Arts and Sciences. Requirements include: The Common Application or Coalition Application, a Penn-specific Essay, Official High School Transcript, School Report, three Letters of Recommendation, a Mid-Year Report, and a Final Report upon matriculation. Standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are also required.
